newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian official targeted in anti-Asian attack.
newsitem.headline: Australian official targeted in anti-Asian attack.

text.p: Vandals smashed the office windows of the Chinese-born deputy lord mayor of Adelaide early on Friday in what appeared to be a racist attack, police said.
The slogan "Go home Gook" and a Nazi swastika were daubed on a nearby building occupied by a fellow Asian-Australian, who is also a candidate for the city council, police said.
They said the two incidents appeared to be linked.
"There's little doubt that it's a racially motivated attack," Adelaide police spokesman Danny O'Mahony told Reuters.
Deputy Lord Mayor Alfred Huang, who has held his position for 18 months and has lived in Australia for 32 years, said he was surprised by the attack on his offices.
"I was quite shocked by the damage," Huang told Reuters.
But he said he did not believe the attack was racially motivated and that Australia remained a tolerant multicultural society.
"I still believe this is a one-off incident as a result of vandalism. I don't believe those views are shared by the majority of Australians," Huang said.
Australia has been racked by a debate about the level of Asian immigration since independent parliamentarian Pauline Hanson said last year that Australia was being over-run by Asians.

Opinion polls showed a majority of Australians supported Hanson's views, but Prime Minister John Howard and other leading political figures have rejected her views and reiterated that Australia would not discriminate against immigrants on the basis of race.
However, Adelaide has long been home to a small but noisy group of neo-Nazi skinheads called National Action who have been responsible for anti-Asian demonstrations and street attacks.
Police said they would question members of National Action over the attack.
